There is no null-safety guard on the decoded request body or the topic list. `RemotingSerializable.decode` returns `null` when the input `data` is `null` (as shown in the dependency), and the `topicConfigList` field can also be `null` at runtime despite the `@CFNotNull` annotation (which is compile-time only). This will cause an unhandled `NullPointerException`:
```java
final CreateTopicListRequestBody requestBody = CreateTopicListRequestBody.decode(request.getBody(), CreateTopicListRequestBody.class);
List<TopicConfig> topicConfigList = requestBody.getTopicConfigList(); // NPE if requestBody is null
// ...
for (TopicConfig topicConfig : topicConfigList) { ... } // NPE if topicConfigList is null
```
A null check on both `requestBody` and `topicConfigList` (returning an appropriate error response) should be added before proceeding.

In the `finally` block, the metrics label `LABEL_IS_SYSTEM` is computed by passing the **concatenated** topic-names string (e.g. `"topic1;topic2;topic3;"`) to `TopicValidator.isSystemTopic(...)`. That method checks `SYSTEM_TOPIC_SET.contains(topic) || topic.startsWith(SYSTEM_TOPIC_PREFIX)`, which will almost always return `false` for a multi-topic delimited string. This makes the `is_system` metric label effectively useless for batch operations. Consider evaluating per-topic or using a different aggregation strategy.

Using `assert` for a critical null-check on the RPC response is unsafe because assertions are disabled by default in production JVMs (`-ea` is not set). If `invokeSync` ever returns `null`, the code will throw a raw `NullPointerException` on the next line rather than a descriptive error. Replace with an explicit null check that throws `MQClientException` or `RemotingException`.
